subject: Onramp initiation — org & network handoff (API keys, IP allowlist, VPC peering)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Ava Summers <ava.summers@synaptech.io>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Onramp initiation — org & network handoff (API keys, IP allowlist, VPC peering)

Hi Ava —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is a first-pass mutual action plan (MAP-SynapTech-v1.xlsx) and a lightweight network template (network-template.pdf) to accelerate the onramp. I pulled out the technical prerequisites we agreed to include in the MAP so we have a single place to track owners and deadlines:

- Org and service account creation (SynapTech owner: infra-admin; Redwood owner: neha_kapoor) — needed to issue API keys and RBAC.
- API keys & ephemeral rotation (Redwood to create initial keys; SynapTech to confirm service account mapping) — target: 3 business days after org creation.
- IP allowlist (SynapTech to provide CIDR list; Redwood will publish IP endpoints) — include both static and NAT egress ranges.
- VPC peering (optional private link; SynapTech to share peering contact & preferred window) — we have a template for the peering request attached.
- Documentation & test plan (shared runbook + smoke tests for token auth) — Redwood to provide smoke test script.

Please confirm owners and whether the proposed deadlines in the MAP file work for your team. If you prefer, we can split the IP allowlist deliverable into "initial" (for demo) and "production" (for full trial).

Attachments: MAP-SynapTech-v1.xlsx (action tracker), network-template.pdf (fields we need for peering)

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm org name and infra-admin (I can create the Redwood side org seed).
2) You send an initial IP list (CSV) so we can configure allowlist for demo traffic.
3) We schedule a short peering window with infra owners (30–45m) once procurement signs MSA.

Thanks — looping in Karthik (infra) and Jonas (solutions) to own technical tasks.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com

From: Ava Summers <ava.summers@synaptech.io>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: SynapTech Procurement <procurement@synaptech.io>
Date: 2029-04-15T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Onramp initiation — org & network handoff (API keys, IP allowlist, VPC peering)

Neha —

Thanks for this and for capturing the MAP. Looks good at a high level. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

- IP allowlist: we can provide an initial CSV with our NATed egress ranges by EOD today. Is there a required column format? We typically send columns: name, cidr, environment (dev/prod), contact.
- VPC peering: procurement wants to see the peering template and the expected timeline for routing changes. We also need the expected AWS account IDs for the peering config.
- API keys / org: infra-admin will be named "infra-admin@synaptech.io" — I will confirm the exact principal tomorrow morning.

Procurement (cc) will also need the MSA and an estimate for duration of data retention (they asked for a short note on logs/audit retention).

We will attach the IP CSV and send the signed procurement note once we align internally.

Thanks,
Ava Summers
Head of Integrations | SynapTech
ava.summers@synaptech.io

Ava —

Perfect, thanks. For the IP CSV format we prefer the simple CSV (name,cidr,environment,contact) — that maps directly to our allowlist import. I've attached a small sample and our peering template (redwood-peering-template.json) to illustrate what we need on the Redwood side (account IDs, routing table, expected prefixes).

Quick owners & internal notes:
- Org seed & initial API keys: neha_kapoor (I'll create the org seed and issue a short-lived API key for demo).
- Ephemeral key rotation & smoke tests: karthik_iyer (infra) — will publish the rotation script and instructions.
- Test plan and support runbook: jonas_weber (solutions) — will produce the step-by-step test checklist and a support ticket template.

Proposed timing:
- Day 0 (today): SynapTech sends initial IP CSV and confirms infra-admin principal.
- Day 1–2: Redwood seeds org, issues demo API key, and configures allowlist.
- Day 3: Smoke tests & short demo.
- Day 4–5: Procurement completes MSA / DocuSign and we schedule peering window (if desired).

I'll open a HubSpot note and a support ticket once we have the CSV. HubSpot link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/87921

Thanks — Karthik and Jonas, flag anything I missed.

Best,
Neha
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Ava Summers <ava.summers@synaptech.io>
Date: 2029-04-16T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Onramp initiation — org & network handoff (API keys, IP allowlist, VPC peering)

Neha / team —

Couple of technical clarifications from infra:

- API key model: we'll issue a scoped API key tied to the org seed. For demo traffic we will enable a short TTL (24h) and provide the rotation helper script (attachment: ephemeral-key-rotation.sh) which rotates via our token endpoint. For production we recommend using the service-account flow (we'll send the RBAC mapping).
- IP allowlist: we only need the egress CIDRs; if SynapTech can include a primary contact per CIDR that speeds up troubleshooting.
- VPC peering: if SynapTech wants to peer, we require the AWS account ID and 2–3 /24 prefixes to accept in the route table. Peering typically takes 2–3 business days to approve with our infra change window.

I'll prepare the rotation script and a short README and attach to the HubSpot record. If SynapTech wants a private link (no peering), we can propose a mutual TLS tunnel — that's a slightly longer engineering lift.

Karthik Iyer
Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Neha / Karthik —

Thanks, all. We're aligned on the approach. Attached is our initial IP list for the demo: synaptech-iplist.csv (columns: name,cidr,environment,contact). infra-admin is infra-admin@synaptech.io.

Procurement has the MSA questions and will route via DocuSign once we confirm a short note on logs retention (we generally retain audit logs for 90 days; we will attach the procurement note to the HubSpot deal).

Next steps from SynapTech side:
- Today: send the IP CSV (done, attached).
- Tomorrow: procurement routes MSA via DocuSign (cc'ed).
- After MSA: we schedule the peering window (Jonas / Karthik to coordinate).

If Redwood can open the support ticket for the peering request (post-MSA) that will help track the change.

Thanks — looking forward to the demo.

Best,
Ava Summers
Head of Integrations | SynapTech
ava.summers@synaptech.io
